docs.title: sq
docs.text:
ktk/sq accepts an endpoint URL for a one-off command:

Command

sq -e http://127.0.0.1:7737/ graphs

docs.title: Configure a project
docs.text:
Place .sq.toml in the project directory. sq also finds it in parent directories, so the configuration applies throughout a repository.

.sq.toml sq.toml

default = "sparqld"

[endpoints.sparqld]
url = "http://127.0.0.1:7737/"

[prefixes]
data = "sparqld:"
schema = "https://schema.org/"

The default value selects the endpoint when -e is omitted. data abbreviates the sparqld: graph names generated from source paths. The project-specific schema value matches the HTTPS IRIs in the example data.

These commands now use the configured endpoint:

sq graphs
sq any
sq -f docs/queries/names.rq

docs.title: Use configured prefixes
docs.text:
sq injects configured prefixes together with its built-in prefix set before sending a query. This query uses both project-specific prefixes:

Source sq-named-graph.rq

SELECT ?name
WHERE {
  GRAPH data:index.md {
    ?subject schema:name ?name .
  }
}

Command

sq -f docs/queries/sq-named-graph.rq

Add -v to a command, as in sq -v graphs, to see the selected endpoint and expanded query. Use sq endpoints to list configured endpoints.

docs.title: Contexts
docs.text:
Consider two YAML-LD documents: one describes Alpha Centauri, and the other describes a person whose comment mentions a planet in that system:

Source alpha-centauri.yamlld

$id: http://dbpedia.org/resource/Alpha_Centauri
$type: http://dbpedia.org/ontology/Star
name: Alpha Centauri

Source guillem-anglada-escude.yamlld

$id: http://dbpedia.org/resource/Guillem_Anglada-Escud%C3%A9
$type: https://schema.org/Person
name: Guillem Anglada-Escudé
rdfs:comment: Led the team that announced the discovery of Proxima Centauri b.

Query the data:

Source triples.rq

SELECT ?predicate ?object
WHERE {
  <http://dbpedia.org/resource/Guillem_Anglada-Escud%C3%A9> ?predicate ?object .
}
ORDER BY ?predicate
predicate object http://www.w3.org/1999/02/22-rdf-syntax-ns#type https://schema.org/Person http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#comment Led the team that announced the discovery of Proxima Centauri b.

The query returns each predicate and value for this person in the default graph. The default context defines the rdfs prefix and maps $type to rdf:type. It does not define name, so JSON-LD drops that property from this source. The discovery announcement credits the person with leading the team that found the planet. An overview of Alpha Centauri describes the planet's orbit around a star in that system.

Keyword aliases such as $type come from the default context. Vocabulary terms such as name need a declared or registered context: project or remote.

docs.title: Default context
docs.text:
$type worked on the Contexts page because sparqld embeds this context and applies it to every JSON-LD, YAML-LD, and Markdown-LD source before the source's own @context. Sources do not fetch it. Turtle and TriG have no @context. Other processors can load the context file from https://sparqld.iolanta.tech/contexts/v1.yamlld. See SPARQL prefixes for the prefixes available to queries.

https://sparqld.iolanta.tech/contexts/v1.yamlld v1.yamlld

# The sparqld default context, version 1.
#
# sparqld applies this context to every JSON-LD, YAML-LD, and Markdown-LD
# source before the source's own `@context`, so the source can override any
# term below. sparqld embeds this file and does not download it.
"@context":
  # Stable W3C namespace prefixes.
  rdf: http://www.w3.org/1999/02/22-rdf-syntax-ns#
  rdfs: http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#
  xsd: http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#

  # Dollar aliases from https://json-ld.org/contexts/dollar-convenience.jsonld.
  # A YAML key cannot start with `@`, so `$id` stands in for `@id`, and so on.
  $always: "@always"
  $base: "@base"
  $container: "@container"
  $direction: "@direction"
  $embed: "@embed"
  $explicit: "@explicit"
  $graph: "@graph"
  $id: "@id"
  $import: "@import"
  $included: "@included"
  $index: "@index"
  $json: "@json"
  $language: "@language"
  $list: "@list"
  $nest: "@nest"
  $never: "@never"
  $none: "@none"
  $null: "@null"
  $omitDefault: "@omitDefault"
  $once: "@once"
  $prefix: "@prefix"
  $propagate: "@propagate"
  $protected: "@protected"
  $requireAll: "@requireAll"
  $reverse: "@reverse"
  $set: "@set"
  $type: "@type"
  $value: "@value"
  $version: "@version"
  $vocab: "@vocab"

A null in @context discards the default and every definition before it.

Listing the address https://sparqld.iolanta.tech/contexts/v1.yamlld in @context records a jsonld:context edge in the file catalog. Applying the embedded default does not add this edge. The embedded context takes precedence over a registration at the same address.

docs.title: Self-registering project URIs
docs.text:
Optional: one file holds the term map and registers a project-owned URI. Parser limits below apply.

alpha-centauri.yamlldcontexts/person.yamlldcontexts/z-dollar.yamlld

Source alpha-centauri.yamlld

$id: http://dbpedia.org/resource/Alpha_Centauri
name: Alpha Centauri

Source person.yamlld

- https://example.org/contexts/combined/dollar
- name: https://schema.org/name
'@type': http://www.w3.org/ns/json-ld#Context
http://schema.org/contentUrl:
  '@id': https://example.org/contexts/combined/person

Source z-dollar.yamlld

'@context':
  $id: '@id'
'@id': https://example.org/contexts/combined/dollar

- http://www.w3.org/ns/json-ld#Context
http://schema.org/contentUrl:
  '@id': https://example.org/contexts/combined/dollar

z-dollar.yamlld is only a nested-registration fixture. Ordinary sources get $id from the default context.

Source materialized-contexts.rq

PREFIX jsonld: <http://www.w3.org/ns/json-ld#>
PREFIX schema: <http://schema.org/>

SELECT ?file ?url WHERE {
  GRAPH ?file {
    [] a jsonld:Context ;
       schema:contentUrl ?url .
  }
}

Term definitions come only from the @context member (JSON-LD context processing).

Source alpha-centauri.rq

SELECT ?name WHERE { <http://dbpedia.org/resource/Alpha_Centauri> <https://schema.org/name> ?name }
name Alpha Centauri Alpha Centauri Alpha Centauri Alpha Centauri Alpha Centauri

docs.title: Bootstrap and paths
docs.text:
• Write jsonld:Context and schema:contentUrl as full IRIs. sparqld retries failed sources when registrations appear. Filename order does not matter.
  • Registration dependencies must be acyclic.
  • Include registration sources in --pattern selection. Reading a body as a context does not load its registration triples.
  • The registered graph is the file that contains the node. Neither @id nor @base selects another file.
  • Relative references inside a requested context resolve from that context's requested URI, so they need their own registrations.

An @context array composes in order. @import requires an object, not an array.

docs.title: Current failure limits
docs.text: With sparqld 0.1.6 and oxjsonld 0.2.5, a recursive relative self-context triggers The remote context stack is invalid. The process stays up, but the HTTP endpoint never becomes ready. Keep this layout restricted until an update resolves the error. Regression tests preserve the expected failure.

docs.text: sparqld does not download context URLs (except the embedded default). An absolute context URI fails until a local registration supplies its body.

• MkDocs

    Expand SPARQL macros into pages during mkdocs build or mkdocs serve.

docs.title: MkDocs
docs.text:
mkdocs-macros-sparqld is an mkdocs-macros pluglet. During mkdocs build or mkdocs serve it starts a read-only sparqld endpoint over a configured directory and expands SPARQL macros into the rendered pages.

This documentation site uses the pluglet for its live SPARQL examples.

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
pip install mkdocs-macros-sparqld

Also install the sparqld binary and keep it on PATH unless you override extra.sparqld.binary below.

docs.title: Required configuration
docs.text:
Register the pluglet with mkdocs-macros:

plugins:
  - macros:
      modules: [mkdocs_macros_sparqld]

Nothing else is required when sparqld is on PATH and the served tree is the project's docs/ directory.

docs.title: Optional customization
docs.text:
Override defaults under extra.sparqld only when you need them:

extra:
  sparqld:
    directory: data                    # default: docs
    binary: target/debug/sparqld       # default: sparqld on PATH
Key Default When to set it directory docs The RDF tree is not docs/ (for example data/) binary sparqld The executable is not on PATH, or you want a project-local build such as target/debug/sparqld

docs.title: sparql
docs.text:
Run a verbatim SPARQL query. A SELECT returns a list of binding dicts (one dict per row, keys are variable names).

{{ sparql('SELECT ?name WHERE { <http://dbpedia.org/resource/Alpha_Centauri> <https://schema.org/name> ?name }') | sparql_table }}
name Alpha Centauri Alpha Centauri Alpha Centauri Alpha Centauri Alpha Centauri

docs.title: stored_sparql
docs.text:
Run a .rq file whose path is relative to the MkDocs project root (the directory that contains mkdocs.yml).

{{ stored_sparql('docs/queries/names.rq') | sparql_table }}
subject name http://dbpedia.org/resource/Alpha_Centauri Alpha Centauri http://dbpedia.org/resource/Centaurus Centaurus http://dbpedia.org/resource/Proxima_Centauri_b Proxima Centauri b

import { QueryEngine } from '@comunica/query-sparql';


const source = { type: 'sparql', value: `http://127.0.0.1:${process.env.PORT}/` };
const client = new QueryEngine();
const bindings = await client.queryBindings(

);
const rows = await bindings.toArray();
const result = rows.map(row => Object.fromEntries(
  [...row].map(([variable, term]) => [variable.value, term.value]),
));

console.log(JSON.stringify(result, null, 2));

docs.title: SPARQL
docs.text:
SPARQL is a query language for linked data. Its name stands for SPARQL Protocol and Resource Description Framework (RDF) Query Language.

  • Cheat sheet

    Common query patterns with results from the Quickstart dataset.

  • Prefixes

    Default prefix mappings and a query that uses them.

docs.title: Cheat sheet
docs.text: The build runs every recipe against the Quickstart dataset. Queries without GRAPH use the union of every named graph, including the file catalog.

docs.title: Select values with prefixes
docs.text:
Declare a prefix once, then select names for three related subjects from the shared default graph.

Source names.rq

PREFIX schema: <https://schema.org/>

SELECT DISTINCT ?subject ?name
WHERE {
  VALUES ?subject {
    <http://dbpedia.org/resource/Alpha_Centauri>
    <http://dbpedia.org/resource/Centaurus>
    <http://dbpedia.org/resource/Proxima_Centauri_b>
  }
  ?subject schema:name ?name .
  FILTER(?name IN ("Alpha Centauri", "Centaurus", "Proxima Centauri b"))
}
ORDER BY ?subject
subject name http://dbpedia.org/resource/Alpha_Centauri Alpha Centauri http://dbpedia.org/resource/Centaurus Centaurus http://dbpedia.org/resource/Proxima_Centauri_b Proxima Centauri b

docs.title: Join related resources
docs.text:
Shared variables join statements about a star and its constellation.

Source alpha-centauri.rq

PREFIX schema: <https://schema.org/>
PREFIX dbo: <http://dbpedia.org/ontology/>

SELECT DISTINCT ?constellation ?description
WHERE {
  <http://dbpedia.org/resource/Alpha_Centauri>
    dbo:constellation ?constellationResource ;
    schema:description ?description .

  ?constellationResource schema:name ?constellation .
}
constellation description Centaurus The closest star system to the Solar System.

docs.title: Keep optional values
docs.text:
OPTIONAL retains rows when a property is absent.

Source optional-values.rq

PREFIX dbp: <http://dbpedia.org/property/>
PREFIX schema: <https://schema.org/>

SELECT DISTINCT ?name ?discovered
WHERE {
  VALUES ?body {
    <http://dbpedia.org/resource/Alpha_Centauri>
    <http://dbpedia.org/resource/Proxima_Centauri_b>
  }
  ?body schema:name ?name .
  OPTIONAL { ?body dbp:discovered ?discovered }
}
ORDER BY ?name
name discovered Alpha Centauri Proxima Centauri b 2016-08-24

docs.title: Filter values
docs.text:
Functions such as LCASE, STR, and CONTAINS narrow matching bindings.

Source filter-names.rq

PREFIX schema: <https://schema.org/>

SELECT DISTINCT ?name
WHERE {
  VALUES ?subject {
    <http://dbpedia.org/resource/Alpha_Centauri>
    <http://dbpedia.org/resource/Proxima_Centauri_b>
  }
  ?subject schema:name ?name .
  FILTER(CONTAINS(LCASE(STR(?name)), "centauri"))
}
ORDER BY ?name
name Alpha Centauri Proxima Centauri b

docs.text:
ASK returns one boolean instead of a result table.

docs.text:
CONSTRUCT returns a graph in the Resource Description Framework (RDF) format, assembled from matching bindings.

Source construct-name.rq

CONSTRUCT {
  <http://dbpedia.org/resource/Alpha_Centauri>
    <https://schema.org/name> ?name .
}
WHERE {
  <http://dbpedia.org/resource/Alpha_Centauri>
    <https://schema.org/name> ?name .

<http://dbpedia.org/resource/Alpha_Centauri> <https://schema.org/name> "Alpha Centauri" .

docs.title: Count triples by named graph
docs.text:
Compare triple counts for three related astronomy example files.

Source graph-counts.rq

SELECT ?graph (COUNT(*) AS ?triples)
WHERE {
  VALUES ?graph {
    <sparqld:examples/alpha-centauri.yamlld>
    <sparqld:examples/centaurus.md>
    <sparqld:examples/proxima-centauri-b.jsonld>
  }
  GRAPH ?graph { ?subject ?predicate ?object }
}
GROUP BY ?graph
ORDER BY DESC(?triples) ?graph
graph triples sparqld:examples/proxima-centauri-b.jsonld 5 sparqld:examples/alpha-centauri.yamlld 4 sparqld:examples/centaurus.md 3

docs.title: Order and paginate
docs.text:
Always pair LIMIT and OFFSET with ORDER BY for stable pages.

Source paginated-names.rq

PREFIX schema: <https://schema.org/>

SELECT DISTINCT ?name
WHERE {
  ?subject schema:name ?name .
}
ORDER BY ?name
LIMIT 2
OFFSET 1
name Alpha Centauri Alpha Centauri A

docs.title: Prefixes
docs.text:
SPARQL queries can use the prefixes from sparqld's default context without declaring them in each query.

Prefix Expanded value rdf: http://www.w3.org/1999/02/22-rdf-syntax-ns# rdfs: http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema# xsd: http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#

This query uses the default rdfs: mapping without a PREFIX declaration:

Source comment.rq

SELECT ?comment
WHERE {
  <http://dbpedia.org/resource/Guillem_Anglada-Escud%C3%A9> rdfs:comment ?comment .
}

Result:

comment Led the team that announced the discovery of Proxima Centauri b.

Declare other prefixes with PREFIX in the query. A query's own declaration takes precedence over a default mapping with the same prefix.

docs.title: Vocabulary
docs.text:
These RDF terms describe context registrations and file catalog metadata.

  • jsonld:context

    Link a source file to the context URIs requested while parsing it.

  • jsonld:Context

    Mark a node as a saved context. With schema:contentUrl, the graph that contains the node registers that URL.

  • schema:contentUrl

    Give the remote URL of a saved context. The graph that contains the node is the local body.
